clue.text: High-handed European politician, Conservative, chasing a lot of perks?

indicators.note: chasing means the following pieces come along behind the trimmed perks
a lot of, not all of, the word perks is used, its tail dropped

parts.note: an MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A haughty Tory Euro-politician is out to grab as many perks as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of perks' is PERKS with its last two letters removed, giving PER, which the rest then chases.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone who acts imperiously, brooking no argument or refusal.

clue.text: Standard finish to Rolls-Royce trim

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level

indicators.note: the finish to a word is its final letter, here of the car name

explanation.surface: A standard finishing trim fitted to a luxury car.
explanation.definitionFit: To trim something is to cut it back by shaving off its edges, a synonym.

clue.text: What Greens will do about revolution?

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a cycle is one complete revolution, as of a wheel

explanation.surface: A question about how environmental campaigners would react to an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests political upheaval, but it is a turn of a wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: Green campaigners famously reprocess waste materials for reuse, so this is what they will do.

clue.text: Changes to some hampers needing adjustment

indicators.note: letters needing adjustment have to be rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A note that some picnic baskets have to be altered.
explanation.definitionFit: Metamorphoses are transformations of form, so changes in the noun sense.

clue.text: Bear's new role in gallery

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the gallery name

parts.note: the Tate is a famous London art gallery

indicators.note: new signals the letters of role made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A bear has been given a new part to play in an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal from the surface, but it is the verb; the Tate is a London art gallery, and 'new' shuffles OLER.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to put up with or endure it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Gets up with a change of heart, and travels

indicators.note: the middle letter, the heart of the word, is swapped for another

parts.note: rises means gets up out of bed

explanation.surface: Someone gets out of bed having changed their mind, and sets off on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: The central S of RISES becomes D.
explanation.definitionFit: Rides as a verb means travels on horseback or in a vehicle.

clue.text: Request sees enjoyment cut by half

indicators.note: the word is cut by half, losing its second four letters

parts.note: pleasure means enjoyment

explanation.surface: A request means enjoyment gets halved.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is an earnest appeal or entreaty, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Youth grabbing a doctor with a number of Brazilian revellers

indicators.note: grabbing says the youth holds the next pieces inside him

parts.note: a lad is a youth
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a medical degree, so a doctor

explanation.surface: A young man seizes a doctor and joins a crowd of Brazilian party-goers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' looks like a count, but it is a musical number: a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The lambada is a sensual dance from Brazil, a number performed by Brazilian dancers.

clue.text: Lingering impression of a fat setter in bits

indicators.note: in bits means broken into pieces, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: The lasting image of a portly crossword setter falling to pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An aftertaste is a flavour that stays after eating, and figuratively any impression that lingers.

clue.text: Reading music?

parts.note: suggests sight-reading a score, but a public performance can be a reading of poems or a programme of music

explanation.walkthrough: The clue wants to be about reading notation; instead it describes a performance, of verse read aloud or music played.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a performance of poetry readings or of music by soloists.

clue.text: Bouncer needing time to replace new carpet

indicators.note: to replace says one letter comes in for another in the word

parts.note: a doorman at a club is a bouncer

explanation.surface: A club bouncer needs time to change a new carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: A doormat is a small piece of carpet-like matting at an entrance.

clue.text: Note things must change with short time for romance

indicators.note: the letters must change their order

parts.note: and is a synonym of with, joining things together

explanation.surface: A letter saying things have to change, as a romance is brief.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-night stand is a brief sexual liaison lasting just a single night.

clue.text: Condensed tune that's piped

parts.note: compressed means condensed, squeezed into less space
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A shortened melody played on the pipes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piped' suggests music on bagpipes, but here it is gas sent along pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressurised gas is delivered through pipes to power tools and machinery.

clue.text: Wrapping instrument with top of handle in glass

parts.note: a cello is a stringed instrument

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the glass

parts.note: a pane is a sheet of glass

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: A musical instrument packed with its handle poking into glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Cellophane is a transparent film used as packaging, so a wrapping material.

clue.text: Deplore charge applied to administrator

indicators.note: applied to means put next to, so the charge goes after the administrator

parts.note: an exec, short for executive, is an administrator
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: Complaining about a fee imposed on a manager.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to detest or denounce something, close to deploring it.

clue.text: Volunteer force surrounding middle-eastern country's capital

indicators.note: surrounding says the force goes round the country

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, is Britain's reserve volunteer force
Iran is a Middle Eastern country

explanation.surface: Volunteer troops encircle the capital of a Middle Eastern country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country's capital' reads as Tehran, but the capital is Albania's.
explanation.definitionFit: Tirana is the capital city of Albania.

clue.text: Suckers seen working for landlord

parts.note: lice are blood-sucking insects

indicators.note: working means put into action, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Parasites spotted at work, bad news for the landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a pub landlord holds the licence to sell alcohol, so is the licensee.

clue.text: Disreputable line that hurts Spain

parts.note: ouch is what one says when something hurts
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A shady remark that wounds Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Louche means shady or of questionable morals, a synonym.

clue.text: Left after dinner, uniform tidy

parts.note: U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to neaten is to tidy

explanation.surface: Someone tidies their uniform after an evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Food not eaten is what remains on the plate when the meal is over.

clue.text: Wants may be shifting whilst accepting income support

indicators.note: accepting says the rearranged letters take the support letters inside
shifting means the letters move into a different order

parts.note: IS stands for Income Support, a UK state benefit

explanation.surface: What someone wants may change while they are on benefits.
explanation.walkthrough: Income Support is a British state benefit; 'shifting' reorders the word to W HLIST so the support can sit after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of things you desire is a set of wants.

clue.text: Abuse mostly coming with popular hormone

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word

parts.note: an insult is verbal abuse
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: Abuse widely linked to a well-liked hormone.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulin is the hormone produced by the pancreas to regulate blood sugar.

clue.text: Public announcements of iron-free meals at last?

parts.note: to press clothes is to iron them
to release is to free

indicators.note: at last picks out the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Wondering about notices for meals that contain no iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'iron-free' looks like a dietary label, but splits into a press and a release.
explanation.definitionFit: Press releases are official statements issued to the media for publication.

clue.text: Relaxes when in view on the way up

indicators.note: in places the word inside the reversed view
in a down clue going up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to see is to view
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Someone loosens up when the sight comes into view on an uphill climb.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on the way up' signals reading bottom to top, giving EES.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease is to loosen or slacken, so the verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Short message, rather quaint

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a tweet is a short message posted on Twitter

explanation.surface: A brief note that is a bit old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee means excessively sweet or quaint, chiefly in British usage.

clue.text: Confirms as attending internationals

parts.note: at means present at, attending
tests, test matches, are international cricket matches

explanation.surface: Someone vouches that they are going to some international matches.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket or rugby match.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness or certify that something is true.

clue.text: Gulp, seeing small hippos do this

parts.note: hippos famously wallow in mud and water

explanation.surface: A gasp at the sight of tiny hippos doing something.
explanation.definitionFit: To gulp food or drink is to swallow it quickly.

clue.text: Bird brought back by golden retriever

indicators.note: brought back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gun dog fetches a shot bird back to its owner.
explanation.definitionFit: An erne is a sea eagle, a crossword favourite among birds.

clue.text: A bit of drama curtailed, 7 perhaps being the dominating power

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of its tail, its last letter

parts.note: a scene is a section of a play
7-down is the lambada, an example of a dance

explanation.surface: A shortened theatrical scene, with a Brazilian dance perhaps, takes over.
explanation.walkthrough: '7' refers to the answer at 7-down; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascendance is a position of control or superiority over others.
